conclusion: In this simulation one long-chat message cost 17.9x the approximate tokens of a short question, so send #2 got a 429 on tokens with 5.9 of 6 requests still free, one agent message planned 10 model calls but without retry sent 7 requests, 6 succeeded and call 7 got a 429 on requests, and with backoff the agent sent 26 requests (16 retries) for 10 successful calls, failed messages went from 3 to 0, and waiting totalled 135.0s across all messages (longest for one user message 52.9s).
setup: simulated clock, seed 21; two token buckets 6 RPM and 10000 TPM (made-up, not a provider's limits), continuous refill, rejected requests spend nothing, input+output tokens charged up front; token charges are approximate (stdlib-only rule: 1 token per started 4 letters, 1 per 3 digits, 1 per symbol, 4 per message), not a provider tokenizer; 3 sends per chat scenario with 5s think time; long chat resends 45 earlier turns; agent plans 10 model calls with growing context and stops at a call that still fails; backoff base 1s, cap 30s, 8 retries, full jitter
